movements.title: Standing calf raise
movements.muscles:
Source body area: calves
What it should feel like: calves working through a full, controlled range
movements.setup: Stand tall with light support nearby. Rise onto the balls of your feet, pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly all the way down.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: calves working through a full, controlled range
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: ankle pain or bouncing through the reps
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use both hands for support and a smaller range.
When this feels easy: Use one leg at a time or hold a dumbbell.
Source regression IDs: calf-raise:reduced-range-beginner
calf-raise:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: calf-raise:tempo-standard
calf-raise:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: ankle pain or bouncing through the reps
movements.equipment:
Variant: none
Base guide: Optional wall/chair support
movements.equipmentSetup: Fixed support nearby. Support must be fixed or unable to tip or slide under hand pressure; do not use movable furniture for pulling.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Chair-supported balance reach
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: ankle, hip and trunk making small balance corrections
movements.setup: Stand beside a sturdy chair with one hand hovering over it. Shift your weight onto one leg and reach the free hand in a comfortable direction, then return to centre before the next reach.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: ankle, hip and trunk making small balance corrections
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: dizziness or a feeling that you cannot recover your balance
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Keep one hand on the chair and make the reach smaller.
When this feels easy: Use less hand support or reach a little farther.
Source regression IDs: chair-balance-reach:reduced-range-beginner
chair-balance-reach:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: chair-balance-reach:tempo-standard
chair-balance-reach:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: dizziness or a feeling that you cannot recover your balance
movements.equipment:
Variant: chair
Base guide: Sturdy chair
movements.equipmentSetup: Sturdy chair. Use a solid non-wheeled chair on a non-slip floor, with feet able to rest flat. Use fixed armrests only where the exercise calls for them.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Dead bug
movements.muscles:
Source body area: core
What it should feel like: deep abdominal control rather than a huge burn
movements.setup: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent. Gently press your lower back towards the floor, then slowly reach the opposite arm and leg away without letting your back lift.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: deep abdominal control rather than a huge burn
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or your back peeling off the floor
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Move only the arms or tap one heel down at a time.
When this feels easy: Reach farther or add a light resistance once control is solid.
Source regression IDs: dead-bug:reduced-range-beginner
dead-bug:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: dead-bug:tempo-standard
dead-bug:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-low-back-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or your back peeling off the floor
movements.equipmentSetup: Exercise mat.
movements.space: Clear mat-length area with room for the full arm/leg reach and a safe route down to and up from the floor.

movements.title: Dumbbell incline bench press
movements.muscles:
Source body area: chest
What it should feel like: chest and triceps working with shoulders staying settled
movements.setup: Lie supported with a dumbbell in each hand, elbows slightly below shoulder level. Press the weights up until your arms are long without smashing the dumbbells together, then lower with control.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: chest and triceps working with shoulders staying settled
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: pain at the front of the shoulder or excessive back arch
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use lighter weights or a neutral grip.
When this feels easy: Increase the load a little once every rep stays smooth.

movements.title: Glute bridge
movements.muscles:
Source body area: glutes
What it should feel like: glutes squeezing hard at the top
movements.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Brace gently, drive through your heels and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a long line; lower slowly.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: glutes squeezing hard at the top
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: cramping in the lower back or hamstrings taking over completely
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Lift only as high as you can keep the ribs down and glutes working.
When this feels easy: Pause for two seconds at the top or progress to a single-leg-supported version.
Source regression IDs: glute-bridge:reduced-range-beginner
glute-bridge:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: glute-bridge:tempo-standard
glute-bridge:standard-advanced

Source caution: acute-low-back-pain

movements.title: Bodyweight squat
movements.muscles:
Source body area: legs
What it should feel like: thighs and glutes working, with pressure spread through the whole foot
movements.setup: Set your feet where they feel natural. Sit your hips back and down as if you are aiming for a chair, keep your chest proud, then drive through the whole foot to stand tall.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: thighs and glutes working, with pressure spread through the whole foot
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: pinching in the knees or back, or heels lifting
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Squat to a chair and touch it lightly before standing.
When this feels easy: Hold a dumbbell at your chest or use a slightly deeper range.
Source regression IDs: squat:reduced-range-beginner
squat:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: squat:tempo-standard
squat:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: acute-knee-pain
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: pinching in the knees or back, or heels lifting
movements.equipment:
Variant: bodyweight
Base guide: Bodyweight or dumbbell
movements.equipmentSetup: No exercise kit required. Use a clear, non-slip floor and stable footwear.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Standing hamstring hinge stretch
movements.muscles:
Source body area: hamstrings
What it should feel like: a mild stretch through the hamstring
movements.setup: Put one heel slightly in front with the leg nearly straight. Push your hips back with a long spine until you feel a gentle stretch down the back of the thigh; ease out and repeat.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: a mild stretch through the hamstring
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: sharp pain, tingling or pulling behind the knee
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Bend the knee more and reduce the range.
When this feels easy: Increase the range gradually without rounding your back.
Source regression IDs: hamstring-mobility:reduced-range-beginner
hamstring-mobility:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: hamstring-mobility:tempo-standard
hamstring-mobility:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-hamstring-injury
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: sharp pain, tingling or pulling behind the knee
movements.equipment:
Variant: none
Base guide: Optional chair support
movements.equipmentSetup: Fixed support nearby. Support must be fixed or unable to tip or slide under hand pressure; do not use movable furniture for pulling.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
movements.muscles:
Source body area: hips
What it should feel like: a stretch at the front of the hip
movements.setup: Take a split stance or half-kneeling position, gently tuck the pelvis and shift forward until you feel the front of the rear hip open. Keep the ribs down rather than arching your back.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: a stretch at the front of the hip
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: pinching in the front of the hip or back pain
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a standing split stance with support.
When this feels easy: Add a gentle overhead reach on the same side.

movements.title: Bodyweight hip hinge
movements.muscles:
Source body area: posterior-chain
What it should feel like: a stretch in the hamstrings and work in the glutes
movements.setup: Soften your knees, push your hips backwards as though closing a car door with your bum, and keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis. Stop when the hamstrings tighten, then squeeze your glutes to stand.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: a stretch in the hamstrings and work in the glutes
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: strain in the lower back
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Practice against a wall, reaching your hips back to touch it.
When this feels easy: Add a dumbbell or kettlebell and keep the same movement.

hip-hinge:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: hip-hinge:tempo-standard
hip-hinge:standard-advanced

movements.title: Wide-grip lat pulldown
movements.muscles:
Source body area: back
What it should feel like: the muscles down the sides of your back and around the shoulder blades
movements.setup: Sit tall with thighs secured. Pull the bar towards the top of your chest by driving your elbows down, pause briefly, then let the arms straighten without shrugging.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: the muscles down the sides of your back and around the shoulder blades
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: yanking behind the neck or shoulder pain
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lighter load or a band pulldown.
When this feels easy: Increase the load while keeping the same pause and control.
Source regression IDs: lat-pulldown:reduced-range-beginner
lat-pulldown:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: lat-pulldown:tempo-standard
lat-pulldown:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-shoulder-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: yanking behind the neck or shoulder pain

Variant: cable
Base guide: Lat-pulldown machine or band
movements.equipmentSetup: Lat-pulldown machine and long bar. Follow the machine setup instructions and user-weight limit; adjust pads/seat and check the pin or safety catches before starting.

variants.name: Wide-grip lat pulldown — Equipped setting (corrected draft)
variants.label: Equipped setting — corrected draft
variants.instructions:
Use the listed specialist equipment in a gym or properly equipped home gym. This is not a minimal-kit travel option. Follow the dose in reps_or_time and this base technique: Sit tall with thighs secured. Pull the bar towards the top of your chest by driving your elbows down, pause briefly, then let the arms straighten without shrugging. What it should feel like: the muscles down the sides of your back and around the shoulder blades
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.

movements.title: Dumbbell farmer carry
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: grip, trunk and upper back working while you still walk naturally
movements.setup: Stand tall with the weight secure at your side or sides. Walk normally with quiet steps, ribs stacked and shoulders level; turn carefully instead of swinging the weight around.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: grip, trunk and upper back working while you still walk naturally
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: leaning heavily to one side or back pain
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lighter weight or shorter distance.
When this feels easy: Walk farther or increase the load a little.
Source regression IDs: loaded-carry:reduced-range-beginner
loaded-carry:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: loaded-carry:tempo-standard
loaded-carry:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: leaning heavily to one side or back pain
movements.equipmentSetup: Two dumbbells and clear lane. Choose a load that can be controlled throughout and place it down securely; do not drop it.
movements.space: Clear level walking lane with space to stop and turn safely; no loose rugs or obstacles.

movements.title: Low-impact marching in place
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: gentle warmth and a modest rise in breathing
movements.setup: Stand tall and march on the spot, lifting each foot comfortably and letting the opposite arm swing. Keep it light and rhythmic — this is movement, not a military parade.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: gentle warmth and a modest rise in breathing
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: joint pain or losing balance
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Hold a chair or make the steps smaller.
When this feels easy: Lift the knees a little higher or add short faster spells.

low-impact-march:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: low-impact-march:tempo-standard
low-impact-march:standard-advanced

Source caution: poor-balance

What it should not feel like: joint pain or losing balance

variants.name: Low-impact marching in place — Easy continuous (corrected draft)
variants.label: Easy continuous — corrected draft
variants.dose: 5 minutes easy continuous movement at a conversational pace.
variants.instructions:
5 minutes easy continuous movement at a conversational pace. Begin and finish gently. Maintain the natural movement pattern; no generic lowering phase, static hold or forced shortened stroke. What it should feel like: gentle warmth and a modest rise in breathing
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.

movements.title: Dumbbell bench-supported single-arm row
movements.muscles:
Source body area: back
What it should feel like: upper back and rear shoulder, not just the biceps
movements.setup: Brace one hand on a bench or hinge forward with a long spine. Pull the weight towards your hip, squeeze the shoulder blade back, then lower until the arm is long again.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: upper back and rear shoulder, not just the biceps
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: twisting through the torso or shoulder pinching
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lighter weight and more support.
When this feels easy: Increase the weight or add a short squeeze at the top.
Source regression IDs: row:reduced-range-beginner
row:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: row:tempo-standard
row:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-low-back-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: twisting through the torso or shoulder pinching
movements.equipmentSetup: One dumbbell and stable bench. Use a stable exercise bench rated for body weight plus any added load; lock its angle and keep it from sliding. Choose a load that can be controlled throughout and place it down securely; do not drop it.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Dumbbell standing overhead press
movements.muscles:
Source body area: shoulders
What it should feel like: shoulders and triceps working while your middle stays steady
movements.setup: Start with the weight around shoulder height, ribs down and feet planted. Press overhead until the arm is long, then bring it back to the shoulder under control.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: shoulders and triceps working while your middle stays steady
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: lower-back compression or shoulder pinching
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lighter weight, one arm at a time, or a landmine-style angle.
When this feels easy: Add a small amount of load without leaning back.
Source regression IDs: overhead-press:reduced-range-beginner
overhead-press:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: overhead-press:tempo-standard
overhead-press:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-shoulder-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: lower-back compression or shoulder pinching
movements.equipmentSetup: Two dumbbells. Choose a load that can be controlled throughout and place it down securely; do not drop it.
movements.space: Clear arm-span area and enough overhead clearance for raised hands and equipment.

movements.title: Forearm plank
movements.muscles:
Source body area: core
What it should feel like: whole trunk working, especially around the stomach
movements.setup: Set elbows under shoulders and make a long line through your body. Brace as if somebody is about to poke you in the stomach, breathe normally and hold only while that shape stays solid.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: whole trunk working, especially around the stomach
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or holding your breath
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use knees down or place forearms on a bench.
When this feels easy: Lengthen the hold gradually or use a lower support.
Source regression IDs: plank:reduced-range-beginner
plank:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: plank:tempo-standard
plank:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-low-back-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or holding your breath
movements.equipmentSetup: Exercise mat.
movements.space: Clear mat-length area with room for the full arm/leg reach and a safe route down to and up from the floor.

movements.title: Floor push-up
movements.muscles:
Source body area: chest
What it should feel like: chest, shoulders and triceps working while the trunk stays braced
movements.setup: Set your hands just outside shoulder width, make a straight line from head to heels or knees, lower your chest between your hands and press the floor away.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: chest, shoulders and triceps working while the trunk stays braced
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: shoulder pinching, sagging through the hips or neck strain
movements.modifications:

movements.title: Reverse lunge
movements.muscles:
Source body area: legs
What it should feel like: front leg and glute doing most of the work, balance challenged but controlled
movements.setup: Stand tall, step one foot back and lower straight down until both knees bend comfortably. Push through the front foot to come back to standing, then change sides.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: front leg and glute doing most of the work, balance challenged but controlled
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: sharp knee pain or wobbling you cannot control
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Hold a wall or chair and use a shorter step.
When this feels easy: Add dumbbells or increase the range gradually.
Source regression IDs: reverse-lunge:reduced-range-beginner
reverse-lunge:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: reverse-lunge:tempo-standard
reverse-lunge:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: acute-knee-pain
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: sharp knee pain or wobbling you cannot control

movements.title: Rowing ergometer
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: legs doing the first big push, then trunk and upper back joining in
movements.setup: Start with knees bent, arms long and body leaning slightly forward. Drive with the legs first, then swing the body and finish by pulling the handle towards the lower ribs; reverse that order on the way back.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: legs doing the first big push, then trunk and upper back joining in
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or yanking with the arms from the start
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use lower resistance and practise the sequence slowly.
When this feels easy: Add short intervals while keeping the same leg-body-arm rhythm.
Source regression IDs: rowing-erg:reduced-range-beginner
rowing-erg:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: rowing-erg:tempo-standard
rowing-erg:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-low-back-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: lower-back pain or yanking with the arms from the start

movements.title: Shadow boxing
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: shoulders, trunk and breathing working together
movements.setup: Stand balanced with hands up. Throw relaxed straight punches into open space, rotate gently through the ribs and hips, and bring each hand straight back to guard.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: shoulders, trunk and breathing working together
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: shoulder pain or wild twisting through the knees
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Keep the punches shorter and slower.
When this feels easy: Add simple combinations or short faster rounds.
Source regression IDs: shadow-boxing:reduced-range-beginner
shadow-boxing:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: shadow-boxing:tempo-standard
shadow-boxing:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-shoulder-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: shoulder pain or wild twisting through the knees
movements.equipmentSetup: Clear floor.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Sit-to-stand
movements.muscles:
Source body area: legs
What it should feel like: thighs and glutes doing the work; a steady push through both feet
movements.setup: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair, feet comfortable and slightly behind your knees. Lean forward a touch, drive through your feet and stand tall; sit back down under control instead of dropping onto the chair.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: thighs and glutes doing the work; a steady push through both feet
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: sharp knee, hip or back pain
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a higher chair or push lightly from the arm rests.
When this feels easy: Lower the chair slightly or hold a light dumbbell at your chest.

movements.title: Upright stationary cycling
movements.muscles:
Source body area: legs
What it should feel like: steady work in the legs and breathing
movements.setup: Set the saddle so the knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Start easy, build to the planned effort and keep the pedals turning smoothly rather than grinding a huge resistance.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: steady work in the legs and breathing
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: knee pain, hip rocking or numbness from a poor setup
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Reduce resistance and duration.
When this feels easy: Add a little resistance or short controlled intervals.

movements.title: Low forward step-up
movements.muscles:
Source body area: legs
What it should feel like: front thigh and glute of the working leg
movements.setup: Put the whole foot on the step. Lean forward slightly, drive through the foot on the step and stand tall on top; lower yourself back down under control.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: front thigh and glute of the working leg
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: sharp knee pain or pushing mostly from the floor leg
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lower step and a hand support.
When this feels easy: Raise the step slightly or add light dumbbells.
Source regression IDs: step-up:reduced-range-beginner
step-up:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: step-up:tempo-standard
step-up:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: acute-knee-pain
Source caution: poor-balance
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: sharp knee pain or pushing mostly from the floor leg
movements.equipment:
Variant: step
Base guide: Step/box and optional support
movements.equipmentSetup: Low stable step and rail nearby. Support must be fixed or unable to tip or slide under hand pressure; do not use movable furniture for pulling. Use a low non-slip step wide enough for the whole foot; avoid chairs or stacked household objects. Keep a rail within reach where listed.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Standing dowel thoracic rotation
movements.muscles:
Source body area: upper-back
What it should feel like: movement through the upper and mid back
movements.setup: Set up on all fours or in a supported seated position. Keep the hips quiet while you rotate through the upper back, following your hand with your eyes, then return slowly.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: movement through the upper and mid back
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: lower-back twisting or shoulder pain
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a smaller range with the arm across your chest.
When this feels easy: Reach a little farther while keeping the hips still.
Source regression IDs: thoracic-rotation:reduced-range-beginner
thoracic-rotation:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: thoracic-rotation:tempo-standard
thoracic-rotation:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-spine-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: lower-back twisting or shoulder pain
movements.equipmentSetup: Light dowel.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.title: Dumbbell overhead triceps extension
movements.muscles:
Source body area: arms
What it should feel like: back of the upper arm
movements.setup: Keep the upper arm steady and straighten the elbow until the arm is long, then return slowly. The elbow moves; the shoulder does not need to join in.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: back of the upper arm
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: elbow pain or shoulder discomfort
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a lighter band/cable and shorten the range.
When this feels easy: Increase resistance or add a pause at full extension.

triceps-extension:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: triceps-extension:tempo-standard
triceps-extension:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-elbow-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: elbow pain or shoulder discomfort
movements.equipmentSetup: One dumbbell. Choose a load that can be controlled throughout and place it down securely; do not drop it.

movements.title: Level-ground walking
movements.muscles:
Source body area: full-body
What it should feel like: breathing a little harder while still able to speak in sentences
movements.setup: Walk at a pace that feels purposeful but sustainable. Let the arms swing, keep your stride natural and choose terrain you can handle confidently today.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: breathing a little harder while still able to speak in sentences
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: chest pain, dizziness or joint pain that worsens as you continue
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Slow down, shorten the route or split it into two walks.
When this feels easy: Add five minutes, a gentle hill or a slightly quicker spell.

walk:supported-beginner

variants.name: Level-ground walking — Easy continuous (corrected draft)
variants.label: Easy continuous — corrected draft
variants.dose: 5 minutes easy continuous movement at a conversational pace.
variants.instructions:
5 minutes easy continuous movement at a conversational pace. Begin and finish gently. Maintain the natural movement pattern; no generic lowering phase, static hold or forced shortened stroke. What it should feel like: breathing a little harder while still able to speak in sentences
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.

movements.title: Wall slides
movements.muscles:
Source body area: shoulders
What it should feel like: upper-back and shoulder muscles working through a comfortable range
movements.setup: Stand with your back against a wall, ribs gently down and elbows bent. Slide the arms upward only as far as you can keep the shoulders comfortable and the ribs from flaring, then return.
movements.cues:
What it should feel like: upper-back and shoulder muscles working through a comfortable range
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
Move smoothly and stay in control.
Keep breathing normally; do not hold your breath.
Use only a comfortable range that you can control.
movements.mistakes: What it should not feel like: shoulder pinching or forcing the hands flat at all costs
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Stand slightly away from the wall and use a smaller range.
When this feels easy: Increase the range or add a light band once the movement is smooth.
Source regression IDs: wall-slides:reduced-range-beginner
wall-slides:supported-beginner
Source progression IDs: wall-slides:tempo-standard
wall-slides:standard-advanced
movements.safety:
Source avoid: none listed (not clearance)
Source caution: acute-shoulder-pain
Stop for sharp, sudden or worsening pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
This is general movement guidance, not injury rehabilitation or medical treatment.
What it should not feel like: shoulder pinching or forcing the hands flat at all costs

movements.title: Armrest-assisted sit-to-stand
movements.muscles: Quadriceps and gluteus maximus; adductors
movements.setup: Sit with hands on armrests.
movements.cues: Push through arms and feet to stand. Use a stable chair against a wall.
movements.mistakes: Heels lifting; knees collapsing inward; dropping onto the seat or forcing extra depth. Exercise check: Use a stable chair against a wall.
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a higher stable seat and both fixed armrests; reduce repetitions before fatigue affects the transfer.
Alternative in this library: Armrest-assisted sit-to-stand. Choose that exercise’s own dose; do not transfer this dose automatically.
movements.safety: Suitability review pending. Stop for pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness; do not force range or train to failure. Use the listed support and comfortable range; seek individual advice for a current injury or an uncertain restriction.
movements.equipmentSetup: Chair with fixed armrests. Use a solid non-wheeled chair on a non-slip floor, with feet able to rest flat. Use fixed armrests only where the exercise calls for them.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.

movements.cues: Step up up then down down. Keep whole feet on platform and no jumping.
movements.mistakes: Rushing; lifting the knees beyond control; adding jumps or twisting the knees. Exercise check: Keep whole feet on platform and no jumping.
movements.modifications:
Make it easier: Use a short seated march or smaller standing steps with fixed support; leave out the arm action initially.
Alternative in this library: Seated alternating march. Choose that exercise’s own dose; do not transfer this dose automatically.
movements.safety: Suitability review pending. Stop for pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness; do not force range or train to failure. Reduce range if the knee position is uncomfortable; do not force painful loading.
movements.equipmentSetup: Low stable aerobic step. Use a low non-slip step wide enough for the whole foot; avoid chairs or stacked household objects. Keep a rail within reach where listed.
movements.space: Clear standing or seated area with room for the listed limb movement; keep supports within reach.
